case_input.Case Information: A 10-year-old female from a rural area in Kendrapada district, Odisha, presented to the pediatrics outpatient department with intermittent abdominal pain, anal itching, and restlessness at night for the past 2-3 weeks. Physical examination revealed no notable findings. Blood and urine tests showed no abnormalities. Her height was recorded at 130 cm and her weight at 29 kg.
case_input.Diagnostic Tests: Examination of the stool samples revealed spherical eggs 70 µm in diameter, yellow-colored, thick-shelled eggs that contained six central hooklets but no polar filaments. Further confirmation was done by examination of another stool sample by the concentration method. Again, the same findings were noted.

attrs.why: Stool O&P twice revealed 70 µm spherical yellow thick-shelled eggs with six hooklets and no polar filaments, and the laboratory physician confirmed this morphology is diagnostic for Hymenolepis diminuta, directly confirming a parasitic intestinal infection. Rural residence and chronic abdominal symptoms remain supportive, and normal physical exam/blood/urine tests do not contradict the diagnosis. Confidence rises from 0.98 to 0.99 because repeated egg visualization plus independent specialist confirmation make the organic parasitic etiology essentially certain.
